articles.title: Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield to Receive £20m for Community Improvements
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale council is set to accept nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising the historically overlooked areas of Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, with plans to improve local facilities and services.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale's Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield are set to benefit from nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising these historically overlooked areas. The Rochdale council is expected to accept the Pride in Place funding at a town hall meeting scheduled for August 25, 2026. This funding amounts to £19.6 million over the next decade, equating to just under £2 million annually.

The funding aims to address various local issues, including tackling congestion, improving parking, creating new green spaces, enhancing local facilities, and expanding maternity services. However, as of now, no specific plans have been established for how the money will be allocated. The council will form a Neighbourhood Board, comprising local community figures and officials, to develop a proposal for the funding's use.

The Neighbourhood Board will include Rochdale MP Paul Waugh and Coun Daniel Meredith, the council’s regeneration lead, and will be chaired by Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group. They have until November 30, 2026, to submit a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, which is necessary to unlock the funding. An initial £150,000 has already been granted to establish the board and generate the plan.

Local residents have expressed skepticism about the funding, citing years of neglect and lack of investment in their communities. Ken Whittle, a long-time resident, voiced concerns about the area's decline, while others have called for better healthcare services and community facilities. The upcoming Neighbourhood Board will aim to incorporate local views into the future plans, with consultation events already held by MP Paul Waugh.

articles.title: Rochdale to Honour Comedian Jimmy Cricket with Lying in State and Funeral Services
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will pay tribute to beloved comedian Jimmy Cricket, who passed away on August 3, with a lying in state at St Patrick’s Church and a funeral service at Salford Cathedral next week.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will have the opportunity to pay tribute to legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket, who died on August 3 at the age of 80 following a short illness. His family was by his side during his final moments. Known for his clean humour and catchphrase 'And there’s more', Jimmy became a household name in the 1970s and was a prominent supporter of local charities and causes in Rochdale, where he made his home.

On Thursday, August 20, Jimmy's body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church on Watts Street from 3pm to 5pm, allowing fans and friends to pay their respects. Following this, a vigil mass will take place at Salford Cathedral at 7pm for the reception of his body, marking the beginning of the celebrations of his life.

The funeral service will be held at Salford Cathedral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21. Mourners are encouraged to wear bow ties, which, along with his iconic Wellington boots, became synonymous with his comedic persona. Jimmy Cricket's legacy as a beloved entertainer and community figure will be remembered fondly by those who knew him and enjoyed his work.

This series of events provides an opportunity for the community to come together to celebrate the life of a man who brought joy to many. His contributions to local charities and the entertainment scene will be cherished, and his passing marks a significant loss for Rochdale.

articles.title: Plans Approved for 23 New Homes on Kirkholt Estate
articles.excerpt: Plans for a new 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses on the Kirkholt estate have been approved, aiming to provide affordable housing for local residents.
articles.content_html:
Plans for a new housing development on the Kirkholt estate in Rochdale have been approved, which will see the construction of a 23-home apartment block and five terraced houses off Queen’s Drive. The developer, Mosscare St Vincent Housing (MSV), aims to provide all homes for social rent, priced at approximately 60 per cent of market rates.

The site, which is currently vacant, previously housed an old block of flats that was demolished in 2009. Following its demolition, the land was briefly used by Kirkholt Medical Practice before the health centre relocated. The planning documents highlight the site as a prominent location within the local area, with the intention of creating a high-quality, sustainable development that addresses local housing needs.

MSV, a not-for-profit Registered Provider, manages nearly 9,000 homes across Greater Manchester, Lancashire, and West Yorkshire. The new apartments will consist of one-bedroom units, while the terraced houses will each have four bedrooms. The development is part of a broader strategy to reduce anti-social behaviour associated with the disused site and to enhance the community by providing affordable housing.

In addition to the housing, plans for a new community garden, to be managed by Q Gardens, have also been approved. This initiative aims to further support the local community and promote engagement among residents. The development is expected to contribute positively to the Kirkholt area by utilising vacant land and fostering a balanced community.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Netball Club Launch New Partnership to Promote Netball
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Netball Club have announced a new partnership aimed at increasing participation in netball across the borough, enhancing community engagement and promoting physical activity.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC, in collaboration with Rochdale AFC Community Trust and Rochdale Netball Club, has launched a new initiative called Rochdale AFC Netball. This partnership aims to enhance access to netball and promote physical activity across the borough, from primary school participation to adult club netball.

Under the new branding, Rochdale Netball Club will become part of the wider 'Our Teams' family associated with Rochdale AFC. The partnership is designed to strengthen the links between schools and clubs, providing a clear pathway for individuals of all ages and abilities to engage with netball. Currently, Rochdale Netball Club supports nearly 200 players weekly, with teams ranging from under-sixes to seniors.

The collaboration will also focus on community outcomes, with plans for new programmes in schools, health and wellbeing initiatives, and volunteer development. By operating under the shared identity of Rochdale AFC, the partnership is expected to attract commercial support and sponsorship, further reinforcing the importance of women's sport in the borough.

This initiative follows a successful model seen in other regions where professional sports clubs have partnered with netball organisations. The priority for Rochdale AFC Netball will be a community-first approach, reflecting the town's sporting pride and welcoming participation from all demographics.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Receives Bronze Award in Fan Engagement Index
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC has been awarded a Bronze Award in the Fan Engagement Index, recognising the club's efforts to connect with its supporters.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC has received a Bronze Award in the Fan Engagement Index, which acknowledges the club's commitment to engaging with its fanbase. The announcement was made on 18 August 2026 via the club's official website.

The Fan Engagement Index evaluates clubs based on their interaction and communication with supporters, considering factors such as transparency, accessibility, and community involvement.

This award positions Rochdale AFC among the top clubs for fan engagement, reflecting positively on the club's efforts to strengthen its relationship with supporters.

The club is expected to continue enhancing its strategies to promote fan involvement and feedback, ensuring supporters feel valued in decision-making processes.

articles.title: Rochdale Council to Accept £20m Pride in Place Funding for Local Improvements
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council is set to accept nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising overlooked areas, including Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, during the upcoming town hall meeting.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is preparing to accept £19.6 million in government funding as part of the Pride in Place initiative, aimed at improving neglected areas of the borough. The decision will be made at the next town hall meeting scheduled for next week.

The funding, which amounts to just under £2 million per year over the next decade, will focus on areas such as Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield. These locations have historically received little financial support for development and improvement projects.

While no specific plans have been established for the allocation of the funds, early suggestions include tackling congestion, enhancing parking facilities, creating new green spaces, improving local amenities, and expanding maternity services in the targeted areas.

The acceptance of this funding represents a significant opportunity for the local authority to address longstanding issues in these communities, potentially leading to improved quality of life for residents. Further details on the implementation of these projects are expected to emerge following the council meeting.

articles.title: Local Golf Clubs Advance to Quarter-Finals of Manchester and District Alliance Competitions
articles.excerpt: Dukinfield, Rochdale, Brookdale and Denton golf clubs have reached the quarter-finals of the Manchester and District Golf Alliance Inter Club Knock Outs, showcasing local talent in regional competitions.
articles.content_html:
Four local golf clubs, Dukinfield, Rochdale, Brookdale, and Denton, have successfully advanced to the quarter-finals of the Manchester and District Golf Alliance Inter Club Knock Outs. This stage of the competition features teams from over 100 clubs across the region, highlighting the competitive spirit and skill present in local golf.

The Dunham Forest Trophy, a key event in the competition, consists of teams made up of a club professional and six leading amateurs. Notably, defending champions Ashton-on-Mersey were eliminated in earlier rounds, paving the way for other clubs to vie for the title. Dukinfield will be led by professional Dave Green as they host Leigh in their quarter-final match.

Other quarter-final matchups include Chorlton facing Dunham Forest, Heaton Moor against Wilpshire, and Wychwood Park taking on Disley. The final of the Dunham Forest Trophy is scheduled to take place at Dunham Forest Golf Club on September 26, 2026.

In addition to the knockout competitions, local clubs have been active in various medal and stableford events. Recent results from Ashton Golf Club saw Andy Lomas win his division after a card play-off, while Brookdale and Denton also reported strong performances in their respective competitions. These events not only foster community engagement but also encourage local talent to shine in the sport.

articles.title: Rochdale AFC Youth Team Begins Cup Campaign
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC's youth team has officially launched its cup campaign, aiming to showcase young talent in upcoming matches. The club is committed to developing players from the local community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC's youth team has officially begun its cup campaign, as announced on August 18, 2026. The team will compete in a series of matches designed to highlight the skills and potential of its young players.

This initiative is part of Rochdale AFC's commitment to nurturing talent from within the community, providing competitive opportunities for young athletes.

Fixtures for the cup matches are expected to be announced shortly, and fans are encouraged to follow the team's progress as they aim for success in the tournament.

Further updates regarding match schedules and results will be available on the Rochdale AFC website.
